summary.why: Two named authorities were never opened during the original build and a third did not exist in that packet. Sixteen defects follow from them: seven from the missing Performance/decision register, nine from other references in reference/ that were also never opened. Every one is a real behaviour, data or vocabulary gap that has now been corrected and re-tested, not a documentation nicety.

prior_omissions.why_missed: The packet's SOURCE_AND_PRECEDENCE_MAP summarised the performance decision in one clause; the summary was read and the authority was not.
Referenced at the packet root by the correction packet but present only at reference/ in the original; the precedence map's summary was used instead.
Absent from the original packet entirely.

defects.defect: No resource/performance manager existed in any concept; 37 builders, none matching perf/resource/governor.
defects.correction: Added manager-performance with behaviour profiles, background policy, byte-budget table, metered/battery/thermal rows, a read-only governor admission table, and an explicit list of what it refuses to expose. Assigned to EVERYWHERE so no concept can invent a second governor.

defects.defect: No ObservableWork projection. pm-sim.js advanced phases on a private timer with five outcome words, no wait reason, no cancel/background/retry, no progress source — the register's definition of fake progress.
defects.correction: New shared/pm-work.js: 24 states, 4 terminal, wait reasons, progress_kind + progress_source, cancel/background/retry only when valid, byte-bounded history, releasable subscriptions. Determinate progress is refused without a real denominator. pm-sim.js now drives operations through it.

defects.defect: onPhase was plumbed through the kit and consumed by no concept, so every operation showed a generic spinner that concealed what was being waited on.
defects.correction: Operation families now declare real choreography (provider_auth, provider_catalog, installation, network, destructive, local), and the shell renders state word, phase, wait reason and valid actions for every live operation.

defects.defect: No virtualization anywhere; every row of every list was rendered.
defects.correction: New shared/pm-virtual.js (windowFor, shouldVirtualize, generations, releasePool). All four concepts window sections above 40 items and state 'Showing N of M'. Verified: 24 DOM item nodes for a 100-record section.

defects.defect: Fixtures below the packet's own performance matrix: 274 settings, 7 installations, 6 MCP items.
defects.correction: New shared/pm-data-scale.js adds provenance-marked volume: 855 settings total, 100 installations, 50 MCP entries, 20 catalogue providers. Authored content unchanged and unmarked.

defects.defect: Receipts were bounded by item count only; 'item counts alone are insufficient'.
defects.correction: Byte contracts on the operation list (64 KB) and receipts (48 KB), plus a per-cache byte-budget table in the resource manager.

defects.defect: No low-resource/legacy profile and no metered-network, battery or thermal behaviour.
defects.correction: Legacy profile plus perf-metered, perf-battery, perf-thermal rows; lowResource demo state drives reduced budgets and degraded permits.

defects.defect: Search exposed 9 record kinds but not setup_workflow or unavailable capability.
defects.correction: Both kinds added to the index with weights and a filter token, backed by 5 setup workflows and 4 unavailable capabilities. Index now returns 11 kinds.

defects.defect: Raw enum strings rendered in normal GUI (channel_not_found, homebrew_formula, pull_request) — 9 occurrences.
defects.correction: Normal surfaces carry human words; exact identifiers retained only in Technical Details rows. Re-scan: 0 leaks in normal surfaces, 6 identifiers preserved in detail rows where the reference allows them.
DISPROVEN — no correction needed. Census showed 'Connect a destination' for hosted services and 'Install a skill/plugin' for real tools; no 'Install <forge>' string exists.

defects.defect: Raw environment IDs possibly rendered in ordinary copy.
defects.correction: Humanized host names added as first-class data (installationHosts); every scale installation carries hostName for display and hostId only as a key. Re-scan finds no host id in any rendered field.

defects.defect: No per-tool acquisition/readiness state family, and the two references conflict over 'Included with this Server'.
defects.correction: 8 acquisition states and 10 readiness words added to pm-semantics.js. The adjudication wins by precedence: acquisitionLabel() refuses any baseline state for a provider CLI unless a named user exception is passed, and downgrades it to 'Available to install'. Non-provider tools such as Git may still show 'Included with this Server'.

defects.defect: Copy Settings From… lacked the restore point / atomic apply / verification contract.
defects.correction: Recorded as an unresolved item rather than silently invented — see unresolved_defects. The existing preview and rollback actions remain; the ten-category transactional contract belongs to the settings lifecycle owner.

defects.defect: Scope vocabulary was 3 of 12 (global, project, thread).
defects.correction: All 12 scopes now present and demonstrated on real rows (turn, Goal, PlanningRun, Crew, host, environment, installation, device, worktree added), with human words via PMSemantics.scopeWord.
7 classes registered with capability flags: pmSecret, vaultReference, pmOAuth, cliOwned, envBacked, helperBacked, nonSecret.

defects.defect: The runtime-demand flow (Provider Setup Required → deep link → continuation token → explicit install → separate auth) was never modelled.
defects.correction: providerCliPolicy and providerSetupDemand fixtures added, including continuation token, stale-continuation behaviour, inspected existing installations, and the explicit 'never installs silently because a Project or Goal wanted the route' clause. 18/18 conformance assertions pass.

preserved_singular_owners.RuntimeResourceGovernor: Only admission owner. Settings reads policy and permit answers and writes policy back; it never schedules. Permit outcomes: admitted, queued, admitted_degraded, blocked_permission, blocked_resource, cancelled.
preserved_singular_owners.ObservableWork: Only progress/wait projection. One renderer in the shell; no concept draws its own spinner.

unresolved_defects.summary: Copy Settings From… still exposes preview and rollback but not the full ten-category transactional contract (pre-copy restore point, atomic apply, verification receipt).
unresolved_defects.why_not_corrected: 01_CORE_ARCHITECTURE and SERVER_BACKBONE §2 both assign the transaction to the settings lifecycle owner. Inventing the ten-category split inside a concept would create a second owner for a canonical flow.

unresolved_defects.summary: Ivy Bridge / Xeon E5 behaviour is approximated by CPU throttling, not measured on the hardware.
unresolved_defects.why_not_corrected: No such hardware is reachable from this environment.

honest_limits: Slow-network load is ~19 s at 400 kbps with 6x CPU throttle. The page ships ~928 KB of uncompressed JS+CSS; that is asset weight, not a runtime defect, and no bundler is in scope.
Old-hardware behaviour is approximated by CPU throttling. This is not Ivy Bridge or Xeon E5 evidence.
Everything network, filesystem or provider touching remains simulated; every ObservableWork projection carries simulated:true.
